separate_source_terms: CREMA-D publisher attribution: Cheyney Computer Science / Crowd-sourced Emotional Multimodal Actors Dataset; ODbL 1.0 database and DbCL 1.0 contents. These separate terms apply to source/derived data, not the project MIT code licence.
Model asset terms are recorded separately in mouth-v4-renderer-assets.json and mouth-v4-renderer-LICENSE.txt.
No source media, generated media, mask PNGs, model binaries or customer data are bundled here.

original_sha256 identifies the publisher FLV; source sha256 identifies the prior matched H264/PCM source, not the downloadable FLV. Source normalization is prepare_video_timing_upgrade.py matched_group at application base 52646e2; rendering/compositing is prepare_mouth_edit_v4.py.

Generated byte hashes identify the actual evaluated files. Library/device/container metadata can change regenerated bytes; record differences and recompute exact changed-pixel masks rather than silently substituting them.
Requested same-frame/earlier mouth ratios are conditioning, not independently verified perfect synchronization or exact achieved output lag.
Actor identities, sentence templates and generator family are consumed; these cases must not be reused as fresh confirmation. No outside reviewer has participated.
limitations: Published inputs identify source positions; actual pixels and model execution need separate acquisition and replay.
The standard-library reviewer checks reported windows, not completeness of window enumeration or track membership.
Generic learned face responses do not establish causal mouth attribution, lip sync, or AI confidence.
Eight consumed actors and one generator family; no independent reviewer has participated.
